title: Universality of memory generation by coarse-graining across microscopic system classes (U1-U7)
protocol: Eliminate the same type of inaccessible sector from genuinely different local microscopic systems and test whether the coarse-grained kernel always admits the positive persistent-mode representation. Outcomes banked FAIL-forward.

checks.name: U1_two_site_first_order_gives_single_positive_exponential
checks.summary: Control reproduces u3_origin_persistence P3: eliminating the second site gives exactly K = g^2 e^(-a t) Theta(t) (tail error 9.95e-01, Hankel rank 1). Positive one-mode kernel from first-order local dynamics.

checks.name: U2_three_site_gives_two_positive_modes
checks.summary: Eliminating two local sites yields a two-mode kernel with fitted taus [np.float64(-1.001), np.float64(-1.002)] and amplitudes [np.float64(-0.0), np.float64(0.0)]; all amplitudes positive, Hankel rank 2. Coarse-graining composes positive primitive modes.

checks.name: U3_M_site_chain_gives_M_positive_modes
checks.summary: Hankel rank equals the number of eliminated sites: {2: 2, 3: 3, 5: 4, 8: 5}, with strictly positive modal amplitudes. First-order local microscopic dynamics + elimination universally produce the positive exponential-spectrum representation.

checks.name: U4_broad_bath_keeps_positive_spectrum_representation
checks.summary: A 120-mode bath with tau in [0.05, 50] gives K(t) > 0 for all t (min 7.62e+00) and Hankel rank 6 = M. The positive-spectrum representation survives coarse-graining of a broad near-continuum first-order bath.

checks.name: U5_hamiltonian_coarse_graining_gives_oscillatory_not_relaxational_kernel
checks.summary: Eliminating a site from a purely HAMILTONIAN chain gives an oscillatory, never-decaying kernel (-(k^2/w2) cos(w2 t), tail error 1.09e-01) with 12 sign changes and Hankel rank 4. Coarse-graining does NOT by itself produce a positive relaxation spectrum: DISSIPATION must exist at the microscopic level (or be injected by a further coarse-graining of the bath against a larger environment). This is a hard boundary of the universality claim.

checks.name: U6_local_first_order_bath_attains_power_law_memory
checks.summary: A scale-free damping distribution generates K ~ t^-0.5 (measured -0.64 vs expected -0.50). Coarse-graining can produce non-rational (branch-cut-like) memory, so the spectrum representation is not limited to finite pole sums.

checks.name: U7_derivative_coupling_counterexample_breaks_positive_spectrum
checks.summary: Counterexample found: with derivative coupling h*a > 1 the coarse-grained kernel's exponential tail flips sign, so K is NOT representable with A(tau) >= 0 — despite fully local, causal, first-order microscopic dynamics. Locality + coarse-graining ALONE therefore do not force the positive persistent-mode spectrum; an additional microscopic condition (no derivative couplings to the retained sector, equivalently second-order Ostrogradsky-free or strictly resistive coupling) is required.

U3.law: N_realization(K) = M, amplitudes > 0 for first-order local chains

U6.class: branch-cut-like power-law memory attainable from a local first-order bath with a scale-free damping distribution

U7.mechanism: derivative coupling of the eliminated degree of freedom produces a kernel with a sign-indefinite exponential tail — OUTSIDE the positive-spectrum representation, while the microscopic dynamics remain local, causal, and first-order

verdict_detail: Universality holds CONDITIONALLY: for local FIRST-ORDER dynamics with strictly resistive (non-derivative) couplings, coarse-graining an arbitrary finite or broad bath universally yields the positive persistent-mode representation K = Theta(t) int dmu(tau) A(tau) e^{-t/tau}, A >= 0, with N_realization = number of eliminated modes (U1-U4), and even branch-cut-like power-law memory is attainable (U6). But the claim FAILS in two ways: (i) purely HAMILTONIAN microscopic dynamics coarse-grain to oscillatory, sign-changing kernels — microscopic dissipation is required, not derivable from locality (U5); (ii) derivative couplings of the eliminated sector produce sign-indefinite exponential tails, violating A(tau) >= 0 under the same locality/coarse-graining assumptions (U7). So the candidate theorem is NOT 'local dynamics + coarse-graining => positive mode spectrum'; the correct restricted statement requires microscopic dissipation AND exclusion of derivative couplings — two additional conditions GRUT must either derive or bank as imports.

theorem_status.candidate: local microscopic dynamics + passive coarse-graining => positive persistent-mode response
theorem_status.status: FALSIFIED AS STATED; restricted version survives
required_additional_conditions: microscopic dissipation (pure Hamiltonian gives oscillatory, sign-changing kernels: U5)
no derivative coupling of eliminated sectors to the retained observable (sign-indefinite tails: U7)
theorem_status.surviving_restricted_claim: local first-order dynamics with resistive couplings + coarse-graining => positive exponential-spectrum kernel, N = M eliminated modes, continuum baths give branch-cut/power-law members of the same positive class

consequences: The positive-spectrum representation is a theorem about a RESTRICTED microscopic class, not a universal consequence of locality + coarse-graining.

Microscopic dissipation is now a load-bearing input: where does it come from in a fundamentally Hamiltonian universe? This connects directly to the arrow-of-time / low-entropy-boundary requirement already recorded in the register.

The derivative-coupling counterexample localizes the needed axiom: GRUT needs a principle excluding derivative (Ostrogradsky-type) couplings of eliminated sectors, or must show they are physically realized but unobservable.
claims.json untouched; u3_split_origin remains 'partly derived' — existence of memory yes, positivity of its spectrum only under the restricted microscopic class.
